newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Feb 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Feb 13.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- The Government is preparing legislation under which British expatriates would have to apply for visas to remain in the territory after April.

-- The Communist Party's Central Committee in Beijing had issued instructions that no major official activities be arranged during Chinese New Year so that leaders could celebrate the festival like ordinary people. Chinese President Jiang Zemin passed the Spring Festival with his family in Shanghai.

-- WEN WEI PO -- A top Chinese economist said that Hong Kong's economy would perform better this year with an annual growth rate of 5.5 percent -- good news for a smooth handover. He also said the property market was unlikely to fall.
-- Taiwanese businessmen in petrol and chemical products, iron and steel and textile businesses expressed optimism on the potential of mainland market.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- The number of people getting married for the first time had been falling in Hong Kong in recent years, with the 1996 figure the lowest since 1980. The main reason lay in the change of the structure of the population. The number of people between age 20 and 30 had been falling.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- One of the chief architects of North Korean communism yesterday became the highest-ranking Pyongyang official to seek asylum in South Korea.
-- China hoped to make new progress on its bid to join the World Trade Organisation at a meeting in Geneva this month.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- A crack police taskforce responsible for security at the handover would leave for Beijing later this month to discuss its preparations with officials.

-- The Hong Kong Stockbrokers Association yesterday hit out at a stock exchange initiative to deregulate brokerage commissions on large orders. It warned that only those involved in arbitrage, warrant and index future transactions would benefit if the brokerage commission was cut.
